Decision: contradicts | WHY: RQCMT-1 and R1 require the later run's progress comment to say it did not start. The design only rewrites the loser's holder record, which is a separate comment, to "not started — concurrent claim". It never touches the progress comment, and it names no change to `core/pipeline/runner.sh`, where the progress comment is started. | ACCEPTED IF: The run that loses the tie-break has its progress comment say it did not start, as well as exiting without removing the label. | QUOTE: Loser: PATCHes its record to "not started — concurrent claim: `<winner>` was first"
Decision: unhandled | WHY: The design relies on reading the issue's comments once and finding every holder record in that read. It does not say what happens when the GitHub comments API pages its results, so a record could fall outside the first page. It also does not say what happens when the loser's PATCH of its record fails, or when the delete of the record on release fails. A stale record left behind would be counted by a later run. | ACCEPTED IF: The decisions say how the one read of holder records covers all comments, and how a failed PATCH or delete is handled (fail clearly, or why it is safe to assume). | QUOTE: It then reads the issue's comments **once** (RQREAD-1).
decision.text:
# Design: Concurrent-claim race detection (issue #2534)

## Decision

GitHub's label API has no check-and-set: two runs can both read "no claim", both add
`zbuild:claimed`, and both get a success reply. After adding the label (gh backend only) the
coordinator posts its holder record synchronously: a comment `concurrent claim by \`<holder>\``
(RQTIE-3, first option; GitHub `labeled` events cannot be the tie-break because a second add of an
existing label creates no event). It then reads the issue's comments **once** (RQREAD-1). That one
read is the re-read (RQREB-1); the labels are NOT re-read (RQREB-2). The first record by GitHub's
`created_at`, then `id`, wins. Other runs' records count only if their `created_at` lies inside
`[own created_at − window, ∞)`. The window is `ZBUILD_CLAIM_RACE_WINDOW_S`, default 120, read on its own
and not derived from `ZBUILD_STATUS_COMMENT_GH_TIMEOUT` (RQWIN-1, RQWIN-2).

- Winner: `{"acquired": true}`; its record stays until release.
- Loser: PATCHes its record to "not started — concurrent claim: `<winner>` was first" (a body that no
  longer starts with the record prefix, so no later run counts it), keeps the label, returns
  `{"acquired": false, "holder": "<winner>", "race_lost": true}`. The engine (`zbuild_claim_acquire`)
  sees `race_lost` and refuses at once, skipping stale takeover (so `_ZBUILD_CLAIM_ACQUIRED` is never set and
  release never removes the label).
- Reply to the POST has no `created_at`: fail closed. Delete the record, remove the label, return a
  backend error. The run's own clock (`date`) is never used (RQFAIL-1). The current code falls back to
  `date +%s`; that is removed.
- Release (`claim_coordinator_release`): delete this run's own record (found by one read, matching
  trusted prefix + own holder), then remove the label, so a later run never counts it (RQREL-1).
- local-fs backend: flock already serialises the add; unchanged.

What already owns the job: the coordinator plugin (`plugins/claim-coordinator/github-labels/`), the
`lib/takeover.sh` pattern for coordinator-side helpers, and ADR-005 §5 (already drafted in the working
copy). The working copy already holds the race helpers in `plugin.sh` (433 lines); the change needs ~40
more lines, so the race helpers move to `lib/race.sh` (as `takeover.sh` is a lib) to keep `plugin.sh`
under 500 lines.

Outside assumptions:
- `rsc_gh`, `jq`, GitHub comments API: already used in `plugin.sh`. A failed read-back or post fails
  closed (record + label removed, backend error).
- GitHub's `created_at` and `id` are assigned at POST time and are stable; once both records are visible
  every run picks the same winner. Known accepted limit (RQLIM-1): if each run reads before the other's
  record is visible, both proceed. Stated in ADR-005 §5 and in the PR body.
- The record format is distinct from takeover notes ("took over a stale claim from"): no interference.

RQTIE-3 is settled by the issue's later requirements (RQFAIL-1 "posting the holder record", RQREB-2 "After posting its holder record"): the run posts its own record.

## Findings
- DSFND-9: the UNCLEAR RQTIE-3 line is removed; the issue's RQFAIL-1 and RQREB-2 fix the own-record reading, and the design follows it.
- DSFND-5, RLREDTEAM-2, RLSCOPE-2: kept as answered earlier; the outside-assumption text still does not accept both-proceed as a result except the stated known limit RQLIM-1, which the issue itself accepts.
- Requirements changed since the last design: RQREB-2 removed the label re-read (DSRACE-7 REMOVED); the others added DSRACE-8..15.

- 1.2 In `claim_coordinator_claim` source the lib, drop the label re-read, fail closed on a missing time (delete record, remove label), and in `claim_coordinator_release` delete the run's own record before removing the label | areas: plugins/claim-coordinator/github-labels/plugin.sh | serves: DSRACE-1, DSRACE-2, DSRACE-8, DSRACE-9, DSRACE-12, DSRACE-14
- 2 `zbuild_claim_acquire` refuses at once on `race_lost: true`, naming the winner, without stale takeover (kept from earlier rounds; check it still holds) | areas: core/claim/claim.sh | serves: DSRACE-4, DSRACE-5

requirements.text:
- RQTIE-1: When two runs claim an issue at the same moment, exactly one proceeds
- RQREB-1: After adding the label, a run re-reads the issue
- RQTIE-2: If another run claimed it too, the run that claimed first wins
- RQCMT-1: The later run marks its progress comment as not started
- RQLBL-1: The later run exits without removing the label
- RQTIE-3: Either the claim writes its holder record itself, synchronously, before it re-reads, or the tie-break uses something that exists at claim time (for example when the label was added).
- RQADR-1: Amend ADR-005: the first claim wins a tie, and how "first" is decided
- RQADR-2: The ADR-005 amendment names its enforcing tests inline
- RQREL-1: A run that releases its claim removes its holder record (its concurrent claim note), so a later run never counts it.
- RQTIE-4: "First" is read from the times GitHub gives the holder records. Records with the same time are ordered by their id.
- RQFAIL-1: If GitHub's reply to posting the holder record has no time, the claim fails closed: the run removes its record and the label and does not proceed. The run's own clock is never used in its place.
- RQWIN-1: Another run's record counts only inside a window before this run's record.
- RQWIN-2: The window is its own setting, ZBUILD_CLAIM_RACE_WINDOW_S, with a plain default of 120 seconds; it is not worked out from another setting.
- RQREB-2: After posting its holder record, a run does not re-read the issue's labels. Reading the holder records back is the re-read.
- RQREAD-1: One read of the holder records finds both the winner and the run's own record.
- RQTST-1: Two real claims run through a fake GitHub: a stand-in gh that keeps the comments and labels our code posts and gives them back when read. No test hand-writes a reply that holds our own holder record.
- RQTST-2: The tests cover the winner, when the two records have the same time and differ only by id.
- RQTST-3: The tests cover the loser keeping the label.
- RQTST-4: The tests cover a reply with no time, failing closed.
- RQTST-5: The tests cover claim, release, then claim again inside the window.
- RQTST-6: The tests cover the window setting and its default.
- RQTST-7: Never touch the real repo.
- RQPORT-1: The coordinator's unit test runs on macOS as well as Linux: no GNU-only sed -i.
- RQLIM-1: The PR states the accepted known limit: if each run reads the holder records back before the other run's record is visible, both proceed.
- RQADR-3: ADR: docs/adr/ADR-005-claim-coordinator.md
- RQSCP-1: Code: plugins/claim-coordinator/github-labels/plugin.sh, core/claim/claim.sh, core/pipeline/runner.sh.
- RQSCP-2: Tests: tests/e2e/claim-race-test.sh, plugins/claim-coordinator/github-labels/tests/claim-coordinator-unit-test.sh, tests/unit/claim-acquire-release-test.sh.
